top_choice_rationale: Mircea Cărtărescu (P001) is my first choice on sustained quality. On public knowledge, which I have not verified and can judge only through translation, his voice is recognizable within a page: long, rhythmically built, hallucinatory prose that joins memory, the body, the city and metaphysical speculation. The Blinding trilogy and Solenoid appear to be built as a deliberate large architecture with a poetic root, not as accumulated episodes. Sem-Sandberg's distinction between recurrence of motif within a developing project and recurrence of method without development persuaded me, and it makes my economy reservation testable against the books. I rank Anne Carson (P002) second. Her line-level control and formal range are real, and a citation limited to original poetry, essay and hybrid narrative answers the translation-scope problem. A durable core beyond Autobiography of Red remains unverified, and Nox depends partly on book design. I rank both ahead of no award (P000), since both rest on a substantial oeuvre with a distinctive voice. The main risk to my first choice is that the late Cărtărescu novels may recur rather than vary. A Romanian-language reader or an anonymous expert report could change my view. Can Xue is not on the slate. I regard her as among the most singular voices on the list, but I cannot show development in her method from this record.
